brussels.title: Jobs in Brussels
brussels.description: Browse EU affairs jobs in Brussels — institutions, NGOs, associations, think tanks and consultancies. Apply on the employer's site.
brussels.html:
Brussels is the political seat of the European Union. The European Commission, the Council, the European External Action Service and most day-to-day work of the European Parliament are here, together with permanent representations, embassies, NGOs, trade associations, think tanks and public affairs consultancies.

EUJobs lists Brussels vacancies across those employers and links each one to the organisation’s own application process. Institutional competitions often run through EPSO or an agency portal; association, NGO and consultancy roles usually use the employer’s form. English is the working language in most EU-bubble offices. French is a frequent advantage, and Dutch or German is sometimes required.

For a narrower search, open a topic page such as public affairs, EU policy, NGO jobs or traineeships, all linked from this hub. Set a job alert if you want new Brussels listings by email.

london.title: Public Affairs Jobs in London
london.description: Find UK public affairs and EU-facing policy jobs in London — government relations, trade, NGOs and consultancies on EUJobs.
london.h1: Public affairs and EU-facing jobs in London
london.html:
London sits outside the European Union, but it remains one of Europe’s busiest hubs for public affairs, government relations and EU-facing policy work. Because of the United Kingdom’s withdrawal from the EU, the European Medicines Agency moved to Amsterdam and the European Banking Authority to Paris, both in 2019. No EU agency is now headquartered in the UK. What stayed is a dense market of people who still need to understand, and influence, EU and UK rules at the same time.

Who hires here

Employers are mainly UK-based, with a strong European regulatory angle:

  • UK government and Parliament — departments, regulators and parliamentary offices that handle trade, competition, financial services, climate and data files with an EU dimension.
  • Trade associations and industry groups — sector bodies whose members sell into the single market or must comply with EU product, digital or financial rules.
  • Public affairs consultancies and law firms — firms advising companies on Westminster and Brussels processes, often with dual UK–EU teams.
  • Think tanks and NGOs — research and advocacy organisations covering Europe, trade, climate, rights and development.
  • International financial and development organisations with London offices, plus corporate in-house public policy teams in banking, tech, life sciences and energy.

The European Parliament maintains a liaison office in London as part of its network outside Brussels and Strasbourg. That supports EU communications and outreach; it is not a substitute for institutional headquarters.

What the work looks like

Typical roles include public affairs manager, government relations adviser, policy officer, regulatory affairs lead and EU affairs specialist. Day-to-day work often mixes UK political monitoring with EU legislative tracking, stakeholder mapping, and briefing boards on how Brussels and Westminster interact. English is the working language; another European language is a frequent asset for association or consultancy posts that serve continental members.

EUJobs lists London openings that connect to the EU affairs community so you can compare them with Brussels and other European cities. Apply through the employer’s own process from each listing. Set a job alert if you want new London posts by email.

berlin.title: EU & Public Affairs Jobs in Berlin
berlin.description: Browse policy and public affairs jobs in Berlin — federal ministries, think tanks, NGOs, associations and EU-facing roles on EUJobs.
berlin.h1: Policy and public affairs jobs in Berlin
berlin.html:
Berlin is Germany’s political capital and a major centre for European and national policy careers. Unlike cities that host a large decentralised EU agency, Berlin’s market is built around German federal institutions, party foundations, think tanks, NGOs and the Brussels-linked advocacy scene that keeps a permanent presence in the capital.

Who hires here

  • Federal ministries and agencies — foreign affairs, economics, climate, digital, labour and related bodies that negotiate and implement EU law.
  • Bundestag and political foundations — parliamentary staff, party-linked foundations and research institutes that shape German positions on European files.
  • European Commission Representation in Germany and other EU communication and liaison presence in the capital.
  • Think tanks and research institutes working on EU integration, foreign policy, climate, digital and social policy.
  • NGOs and advocacy networks — German and European civil society with Berlin headquarters or advocacy offices.
  • Trade associations and corporate public affairs — industry federations and company government-relations teams covering Berlin and Brussels.
  • Public affairs consultancies advising on German and EU legislative processes.

Berlin does not host the headquarters of a major decentralised EU agency. Germany’s agency seats include the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) in Cologne and, in Frankfurt, the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) and the Authority for Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AMLA). The European Central Bank is in Frankfurt as well. Most “EU affairs” roles in Berlin are therefore national-facing with a European portfolio, or dual-location with Brussels.

Languages and profiles

German is often required or strongly preferred for ministry-adjacent and association roles; English is standard in international NGOs, think tanks and corporate EU affairs. Common titles include policy officer, Referent/in, public affairs manager, advocacy lead and programme officer.

paris.title: EU Agency & Public Affairs Jobs Paris
paris.description: Find EU and public affairs jobs in Paris — EBA, ESMA, ministries, think tanks, associations and consultancies on EUJobs.
paris.h1: EU affairs and public affairs jobs in Paris
paris.html:
Paris combines a national political capital with European supervisory authorities for financial markets. If you are looking for EU-linked careers in France’s capital, you will see institutional agency roles alongside classic French public affairs, associations and think tanks.

EU bodies actually based in Paris

Verified seats include:

  • European Banking Authority (EBA) — EU banking regulation and supervision standards. It moved from London to Paris in 2019 because of the United Kingdom’s withdrawal from the EU.
  • European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) — EU securities markets authority.
  • European Union Institute for Security Studies (EUISS) — EU agency for security and defence analysis.

These sit alongside ministries, regulators and market participants who engage with EU financial, digital and industrial files every week.

Other employers

  • French ministries and independent regulators that transpose and negotiate EU law.
  • Think tanks and research centres on European affairs, economics and foreign policy.
  • Trade associations and corporate public affairs teams in finance, energy, tech, transport and other regulated sectors.
  • NGOs and international advocacy offices with Paris bases.
  • Public affairs and strategy consultancies bridging Paris and Brussels.

What to expect

Agency posts at EBA and ESMA often require specialised knowledge of financial regulation, risk or markets, plus eligibility rules that differ from private-sector public affairs roles. Association and consultancy jobs look more like classic EU public affairs: monitoring, advocacy, member briefings and stakeholder engagement. French is frequently essential for national advocacy; English is the working language in many EU agency and international settings.

geneva.title: UN & International Jobs in Geneva
geneva.description: Explore international organisation and multilateral policy jobs in Geneva — UN, trade, health and humanitarian roles on EUJobs.
geneva.html:
Geneva is outside the European Union. Its job market is defined by the United Nations system and other multilateral organisations, not by EU institutions or decentralised EU agencies. EUJobs includes Geneva because many EU-affairs professionals move between Brussels and the multilateral world — and because EU policy on trade, health, human rights and humanitarian aid is shaped in negotiations here every day.

Who is based in Geneva

Major headquarters and permanent presence include (non-exhaustive):

  • United Nations Office at Geneva (UNOG) and other UN entities based there (for example UNHCR, UNCTAD and UNECE).
  • World Health Organization (WHO), International Labour Organization (ILO), World Trade Organization (WTO), World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
  • International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).
  • Permanent missions of states, NGOs, research institutes and consultancies clustered around the international district.

There is no EU agency headquarters in Geneva. EU engagement happens through delegations, member-state missions and thematic cooperation with these organisations.

Career patterns

Roles range from political affairs and programme management to legal, communications, partnership and technical specialist posts. Recruitment often runs through organisation-specific portals with nationality, language and grade rules. French and English are both widely used; additional UN languages help. Many professionals combine Geneva experience with earlier EU bubble work on trade, health, asylum or development files.

EUJobs surfaces Geneva openings that are relevant to the European policy community. Check each listing for contract type, grade and how to apply on the organisation’s own site. Job alerts are useful because multilateral vacancies open on irregular calendars.

luxembourg.title: EU Institution Jobs in Luxembourg
luxembourg.description: Browse EU institution and finance jobs in Luxembourg — Court of Justice, EIB, Commission services and related roles on EUJobs.
luxembourg.h1: EU institution and policy jobs in Luxembourg
luxembourg.html:
Luxembourg is one of the European Union’s institutional seats. Alongside Brussels and Strasbourg, it hosts courts, financial institutions and significant Commission services — a career market that feels more institutional and finance-oriented than the association-heavy Brussels bubble.

EU institutions and bodies based in Luxembourg

Verified presence includes:

  • Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU)
  • European Court of Auditors (ECA)
  • European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO)
  • Translation Centre for the Bodies of the EU (CdT) and the Euratom Supply Agency
  • European Commission departments housed in Luxembourg, including Eurostat, and the Publications Office of the EU
  • European Parliament — Protocol No 6 places the General Secretariat in Luxembourg. Plenary sessions are held in Strasbourg and committees meet in Brussels.
  • European Investment Bank (EIB) and European Investment Fund (EIF)

The European Stability Mechanism (ESM) is also headquartered in Luxembourg. It is an intergovernmental organisation of the euro-area countries, not an EU institution. The European Financial Stability Facility (EFSF) is based in Luxembourg too. It is a euro-area facility, not an EU institution.

Under Protocol No 6, the Council’s seat is Brussels. During April, June and October, the Council holds its meetings in Luxembourg.

What the market feels like

Many roles are institutional: lawyer-linguists, administrators, auditors, statisticians, translators, finance specialists and IT or security profiles. Private-sector public affairs is smaller than in Brussels, but banking, funds and advisory firms hire EU-aware compliance, policy and communications talent around Kirchberg. French, German and English all matter in daily work; Luxembourgish appears in some local contexts.

If you want court, audit, investment-bank or Commission-service careers with a clear EU label, Luxembourg is a primary destination. Competition paths often go through EPSO or the institution’s own vacancy portal rather than a generic consultancy CV drop. Browse current listings on EUJobs and apply through the employer or competition link named in each advert. Alerts help you catch specialised legal and finance openings when they appear.

strasbourg.title: EU & Council of Europe Jobs Strasbourg
strasbourg.description: Find European Parliament, Council of Europe and human-rights policy jobs in Strasbourg listed on EUJobs.
strasbourg.h1: European and human-rights jobs in Strasbourg
strasbourg.html:
Strasbourg is a European capital of a different kind: the official seat of the European Parliament for monthly plenary sessions, and home to the Council of Europe and the European Court of Human Rights. The city mixes EU parliamentary work with a wider human-rights and intergovernmental ecosystem that is not the same as the Brussels Commission–Council bubble.

Institutions to know

  • European Parliament — Under the treaties, the Parliament has its seat in Strasbourg, where the twelve periods of monthly plenary sessions, including the budget session, are held. Committees and additional sittings take place in Brussels; the General Secretariat remains in Luxembourg. Plenary weeks shape short-term staffing, media and logistics demand in the city.
  • Council of Europe — A separate international organisation, not an EU institution, focused on human rights, democracy and the rule of law.
  • European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) — The Court of the Council of Europe, based in Strasbourg. It is not an EU court; that role belongs to the Court of Justice of the EU in Luxembourg.
  • European Ombudsman — EU body seated in Strasbourg, with an office in Brussels as well. It investigates maladministration by EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.

Diplomatic missions, NGOs, academic institutes and service providers support these institutions year-round.

Career angles

Parliament-related roles may be institutional — officials or accredited assistants during sessions — or satellite work in communications, events, interpretation support and local associations. Council of Europe and ECHR careers follow those organisations’ own staff rules. French and English are central; German is useful in the Alsace context. There is no cluster of decentralised EU agency headquarters here comparable to Paris or Amsterdam. eu-LISA, the EU agency for large-scale IT systems in justice and home affairs, has its operational site in Strasbourg; its headquarters are in Tallinn.

EUJobs lists Strasbourg openings for people who want parliamentary, human-rights or European civic careers. Always confirm whether a role is EU, Council of Europe or local — the employer type and contract rules differ. Use alerts around plenary periods if you chase short-term session support roles.

the-hague.title: Europol & Eurojust Jobs in The Hague
the-hague.description: Browse justice, security and international policy jobs in The Hague — Europol, Eurojust, OPCW and related roles on EUJobs.
the-hague.h1: Justice, security and policy jobs in The Hague
the-hague.html:
The Hague is the Netherlands’ city of international law, justice and security cooperation. For EU-affairs candidates, it is best known as the seat of Europol and Eurojust, with a broader international zone that also hosts non-EU organisations active on peace, disarmament and justice.

EU agencies based here

  • Europol — European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation.
  • Eurojust — European Union Agency for Criminal Justice Cooperation.

Both sit in The Hague’s international district and recruit specialists in policing cooperation, judicial cooperation, data protection, analysis, legal services and corporate functions.

Other international employers

  • Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) — an international organisation headquartered in The Hague (not an EU agency).
  • International courts and legal institutions in the city, plus Dutch ministries for foreign affairs and justice and security that work daily with EU justice and home affairs files.
  • NGOs, think tanks and consultancies focused on peace, justice, cyber and security policy.

Amsterdam hosts the European Medicines Agency. Do not confuse the two Dutch cities when targeting applications.

Profiles in demand

Agency vacancies often ask for law-enforcement, judicial, intelligence-analysis, IT security or legal backgrounds, and some functions require eligibility for security clearance. Policy and communications roles also exist around the international organisations. English is widely used inside the agencies; Dutch helps for national ministry and local association posts.

Search The Hague listings on EUJobs when your path is justice and home affairs rather than classic single-market public affairs in Brussels. Read each advert for contract type and clearance expectations before you apply, and set alerts for agency keywords you care about.

vienna.title: FRA & International Jobs in Vienna
vienna.description: Find EU Agency for Fundamental Rights and international organisation jobs in Vienna — UN, OSCE and policy roles on EUJobs.
vienna.h1: EU and international organisation jobs in Vienna
vienna.html:
Vienna combines an EU agency seat with one of Europe’s densest United Nations and security-organisation hubs. Candidates often choose it for fundamental rights, nuclear, drugs and security policy careers rather than classic Brussels association work.

EU presence

  • European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights (FRA) — decentralised EU agency headquartered in Vienna.

Austria’s capital also hosts the European Commission’s representation and the usual pattern of EU-related communications and liaison work that you find in member-state capitals.

International organisations

The Vienna International Centre hosts major organisations including:

  • United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and other UN entities at the centre
  • International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)

The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) Secretariat is also in Vienna, at Wallnerstrasse in the city centre. It is not based at the Vienna International Centre.

These are international or UN-system employers, not EU agencies, but their policy agendas overlap heavily with EU external action, justice and home affairs, and non-proliferation.

Local ecosystem

Austrian federal ministries, party academies, NGOs, research institutes and corporate public affairs teams round out the market. German is important for national roles; English dominates in FRA and most international organisations. Multilingual CVs are common, and many professionals move between Vienna’s international campus and Brussels over a career.

EUJobs groups Vienna openings so you can see FRA, international-organisation and Austrian policy roles in one place. Read each advert carefully for whether recruitment is via an EU agency portal, a UN system process or a national employer. Alerts are useful because IO vacancy windows can be short.

When you browse Vienna on EUJobs, treat FRA posts and UN/OSCE posts as different tracks with different portals — then decide whether your next move is rights-focused EU agency work or the wider international campus.

madrid.title: Public Affairs Jobs in Madrid
madrid.description: Browse policy and public affairs jobs in Madrid — ministries, associations, think tanks, NGOs and EU-facing roles on EUJobs.
madrid.h1: Policy and public affairs jobs in Madrid
madrid.html:
Madrid is Spain’s political and corporate capital. It does not host the headquarters of a major decentralised EU agency — Spain’s agency seats include EUIPO in Alicante, EU-OSHA in Bilbao and the EU Satellite Centre in Torrejón de Ardoz near Madrid. The city’s European careers are therefore built around national institutions, representation offices and advocacy, with strong links to Brussels.

Who hires here

  • Spanish ministries and regulators negotiating and implementing EU law across economy, energy, digital, labour and environment.
  • European Commission Representation in Spain and European Parliament liaison presence.
  • Think tanks and academic centres on European affairs and foreign policy.
  • Trade associations and business organisations representing Spanish industry toward Madrid and Brussels.
  • NGOs and foundations with Spanish headquarters and EU advocacy portfolios.
  • Corporate public affairs and consultancies serving companies that need both Spanish political intelligence and EU regulatory tracking.

How the work differs from Brussels

In Madrid you are closer to the Spanish Council position and to domestic implementation; Brussels remains the venue for day-to-day institutional lobbying. Many mid-career professionals split time, language and networks between the two cities. Spanish is typically required for ministry and national association roles; English is expected for EU-facing briefs and multinational teams. French or Portuguese can help in Iberian and EU coalition work.

rome.description: Find FAO, WFP, IFAD and Italian public affairs jobs in Rome — food, development and EU-facing policy roles on EUJobs.
rome.h1: International organisation and public affairs jobs in Rome
rome.html:
Rome is unusual among EU capitals: its global brand in the policy job market is United Nations food and agriculture agencies, while classic decentralised EU agencies sit elsewhere in Italy — for example EFSA in Parma and the European Training Foundation in Turin.

International organisations headquartered in Rome

  • Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
  • World Food Programme (WFP)
  • International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)

The EU maintains a delegation relationship with these Rome-based UN agencies. Development, agriculture, food security and humanitarian careers often run through these headquarters.

EU and Italian public affairs

  • European Commission Representation in Italy in Rome, plus related EU communication presence.
  • Italian ministries and Parliament dealing with EU files.
  • Think tanks, NGOs, trade associations and corporate public affairs teams covering energy, agri-food, industry and Mediterranean policy.
  • Consultancies bridging Rome and Brussels.

There is no large EU agency headquarters in Rome itself. Do not confuse UN agency vacancies with EPSO or EU-agency competitions — the application portals and eligibility rules differ.

Languages and paths

English and Italian are both widely used; French or Spanish help in UN and Mediterranean contexts. Profiles range from programme and partnership officers in the UN system to Italian government-relations and EU affairs roles in the private and non-profit sectors.

EUJobs lists Rome openings relevant to European and international policy professionals. Check each posting for the correct application portal — UN, EU representation or employer site — and use alerts if you are watching food-security or development keywords.

warsaw.description: Browse Frontex and public affairs jobs in Warsaw — border agency, ministries, NGOs and EU-facing roles on EUJobs.
warsaw.h1: Frontex and public affairs jobs in Warsaw
warsaw.html:
Warsaw hosts the headquarters of Frontex, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency — one of the EU’s most operational decentralised agencies. That gives the Polish capital a distinctive justice-and-home-affairs flavour alongside the usual national policy market of a large member-state capital.

EU agency seat

  • Frontex (European Border and Coast Guard Agency) — headquartered in Warsaw. Roles span operational cooperation, analysis, fundamental-rights monitoring, legal services, procurement, IT and corporate functions, subject to agency eligibility and security rules.

Other employers

  • Polish ministries and agencies implementing Schengen, migration, security and single-market files.
  • European Commission Representation in Poland and EU-related communications work.
  • NGOs and foundations active on rule of law, migration, democracy and civil society — often with strong Brussels links.
  • Think tanks and research institutes on European and security policy.
  • Trade associations and corporate public affairs in energy, tech, defence-adjacent and industrial sectors.
  • Consultancies advising on Polish and EU regulatory processes.

Practical notes

English is widely used inside Frontex and international NGOs; Polish is typically required for national ministry and many association roles. Agency competitions differ from private-sector public affairs hiring — read grade, contract type and nationality rules carefully. Security-sensitive functions may involve clearance processes that lengthen recruitment timelines.

Use EUJobs to find Warsaw listings across Frontex-related, NGO and public affairs paths, then apply on the employer’s own site. Alerts help if you are tracking both agency and civil-society openings.

copenhagen.h1: Environment agency and policy jobs in Copenhagen
copenhagen.html:
Copenhagen is home to the European Environment Agency (EEA) and to a Danish policy scene that punches above its weight on climate, energy and green industrial strategy. For environment-focused EU careers outside Brussels, it is a primary destination.

EU agency seat

  • European Environment Agency (EEA) — decentralised EU agency based in Copenhagen. It provides environmental information and assessments to support EU and national policymaking. Vacancies typically cover scientific analysis, data, communications, IT and administrative profiles under agency staff rules.

Wider employer mix

  • Danish ministries and agencies on climate, energy, environment and food — closely tied to EU Green Deal and related files.
  • European Commission Representation in Denmark.
  • NGOs and advocacy groups on climate, nature and sustainability, often cooperating with Brussels networks.
  • Think tanks and research organisations, including technical institutes that feed Nordic and EU debates.
  • Trade associations and corporate sustainability or public affairs teams in energy, shipping, agri-food and cleantech.
  • Consultancies with Nordic–EU regulatory practices.

Languages and how to search

English is the working language at the EEA and in many international NGOs; Danish is important for national advocacy and some ministry-adjacent roles. Other Nordic or EU languages are a plus for regional coalition work.

stockholm.description: Browse ECDC and public affairs jobs in Stockholm — health security, ministries, NGOs and EU-facing roles on EUJobs.
stockholm.h1: ECDC and public affairs jobs in Stockholm
stockholm.html:
Stockholm hosts the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), giving the Swedish capital a clear EU health-security specialism. Around it sits a high-trust national policy market strong on life sciences, digital and climate files.

EU agency seat

  • ECDC — decentralised EU agency headquartered in Stockholm. It works on surveillance, scientific advice and coordination related to infectious disease threats. Recruitment covers epidemiology, public health, data science, communication and support functions under EU agency conditions.

Other employers

  • Swedish ministries and agencies for public health, social affairs, enterprise, climate and digital policy that negotiate EU legislation.
  • European Commission Representation in Sweden.
  • Life-sciences and health industry associations and corporate government-affairs teams.
  • NGOs and foundations on health, rights, environment and development.
  • Think tanks and academic policy centres.
  • Public affairs consultancies serving Nordic clients with Brussels exposure.

Career tips

Scientific and public-health credentials matter for many ECDC posts; classic public affairs skills matter more in associations and corporate roles. English is standard in the agency and international NGOs; Swedish is often required for domestic public affairs. Neighbouring Nordic capitals — for example Copenhagen with the EEA — are part of the same talent circuit for environment and health specialists.

Find Stockholm listings on EUJobs and apply through the portal named by each employer. Use alerts if you are watching health-security or life-sciences regulatory keywords across the Nordics.

Health-security and life-sciences profiles fit Stockholm especially well because of ECDC and Sweden’s industry base. Keep agency and corporate/NGO searches separate — the skill mix overlaps, the hiring rules do not.

EU agency seat

lisbon.title: EMSA, EUDA & Policy Jobs Lisbon
lisbon.description: Browse EMSA, EUDA and public affairs jobs in Lisbon — maritime, drugs agency and EU-facing policy roles on EUJobs.
lisbon.h1: EU agency and public affairs jobs in Lisbon
lisbon.html:
Lisbon is one of the few capitals with two decentralised EU agencies on its territory, plus a growing Portuguese public affairs and tech-policy scene connected to Brussels.

EU agencies based in Lisbon

  • European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA) — maritime safety, pollution preparedness and related EU tasks.
  • European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA) — decentralised EU agency on drugs, based in Lisbon. It replaced the European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction (EMCDDA) on 2 July 2024.

Both recruit technical, analytical, legal, communications and administrative profiles under EU agency staff regulations.

Other employers

  • Portuguese ministries and regulators on transport, the sea economy, justice, health and digital policy.
  • European Commission Representation in Portugal.
  • NGOs and foundations active on social policy, migration, environment and European democracy.
  • Trade associations and corporate public affairs, including energy, tourism, maritime and tech.
  • Consultancies and research centres with Lusophone and EU networks.

Languages and search tips

English is widely used inside the agencies; Portuguese is typically needed for national advocacy and many ministry-facing roles. Spanish or French can help in Iberian and EU coalition work. Maritime, logistics and public-health backgrounds are especially relevant for EMSA and EUDA tracks; classic monitoring and advocacy skills matter more in associations.

Search Lisbon openings on EUJobs if you want maritime, drugs-policy or Portuguese EU affairs careers — then apply on the agency or employer site linked from each vacancy. Set alerts for the agency acronyms if those are your primary targets.

athens.title: ENISA & Policy Jobs in Athens
athens.description: Find ENISA and Greek public affairs jobs in Athens — EU cybersecurity agency, ministries and EU-facing roles on EUJobs.
athens.h1: ENISA and public affairs jobs in Athens
athens.html:
Athens is the headquarters city of ENISA, the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity — a clear EU specialism in a capital that also runs Greece’s national European policy machinery.

EU agency seat

  • ENISA (European Union Agency for Cybersecurity) — day-to-day headquarters in Chalandri, Athens, plus a local office in Brussels. The agency works on cybersecurity policy support, capacity building and cooperation across the Union. The EU Interinstitutional Style Guide still lists the seat as Heraklion under the 2019 Cybersecurity Act. ENISA’s own contact page and the EU institutions directory describe Athens as the headquarters. A Management Board decision of June 2024 set 30 June 2026 as the date to close the Heraklion office. ENISA’s main contact page no longer lists Heraklion, but some official pages still mentioned that office in 2026, so confirm the duty station on the vacancy. A January 2026 Commission proposal, not yet adopted, would name Athens as the legal seat. Roles include cybersecurity experts, policy officers and corporate functions under agency staff rules.

Greece also hosts Cedefop in Thessaloniki for vocational training — relevant to Greek EU careers but not an Athens headquarters.

Other employers

  • Greek ministries and regulators on digital, telecoms, economy, shipping and migration files with heavy EU content.
  • European Commission Representation in Greece.
  • NGOs and foundations on rights, migration, environment and European affairs.
  • Trade associations and corporate public affairs, including shipping, energy, tourism and tech.
  • Think tanks, academic centres and consultancies bridging Athens and Brussels.

Languages

English is widely used at ENISA; Greek is usually needed for national public affairs. Cybersecurity and digital-policy credentials are distinctive advantages for agency and corporate regulatory roles. Shipping and energy backgrounds also travel well in the Greek advocacy market.

Search Athens listings on EUJobs when your target is cybersecurity, digital policy or Greek EU affairs — then apply on the linked employer site. Alerts for “ENISA” or “cybersecurity” keep you current without daily browsing.

ENISA’s Athens headquarters is the clearest EU-agency reason to target the city for cybersecurity careers. Pair that search with Greek ministry and association roles if you want a broader digital-policy path.

amsterdam.h1: EMA and public affairs jobs in Amsterdam
amsterdam.html:
Amsterdam became a major EU agency city when the European Medicines Agency (EMA) moved from London in 2019, because of the United Kingdom’s withdrawal from the EU. The city now anchors EU medicines regulation alongside a Dutch corporate and NGO scene strong on life sciences, tech and sustainability.

EU agency seat

  • European Medicines Agency (EMA) — decentralised EU agency headquartered in Amsterdam since 2019. It evaluates and supervises medicines for human and veterinary use across the EU. Vacancies cover scientific assessment, regulatory procedures, data, communications and administration under EU agency conditions.

For justice and home affairs agencies — Europol and Eurojust — look at The Hague, not Amsterdam.

Other employers

  • Dutch ministries and regulators for health, economic affairs, digital and climate policy, with close EMA and EU single-market ties.
  • National EU representation and liaison work in the Netherlands, which often involves Amsterdam-based industry and NGOs even when some offices sit in The Hague.
  • Pharma, biotech and medtech in-house regulatory and public affairs teams.
  • NGOs and patient organisations on health and research policy.
  • Trade associations, think tanks and consultancies with Benelux–Brussels practices.

Languages

English is the working language at EMA and in many international health organisations; Dutch is important for national advocacy. Scientific or regulatory affairs backgrounds are especially relevant for agency and industry roles; monitoring and stakeholder skills matter more in associations and consultancies.

Browse Amsterdam openings on EUJobs to compare EMA, industry and advocacy paths. Apply via each listing’s employer link, and set alerts if medicines regulation is your primary search.

EMA dominates Amsterdam’s EU-agency story; keep The Hague in mind if your profile is justice and police cooperation instead. EUJobs city pages are meant to make that geography clear before you apply.

milan.description: Find corporate public affairs and EU-facing policy jobs in Milan — industry, finance, associations and consultancies on EUJobs.
milan.h1: Corporate public affairs and EU-facing jobs in Milan
milan.html:
Milan is Italy’s business and finance capital, not the seat of a decentralised EU agency. Italy’s agency geography includes EFSA in Parma and the European Training Foundation in Turin; Rome hosts the UN food agencies. Milan’s European job market is therefore corporate public affairs, associations and professional services with a strong Brussels connection.

Who hires here

  • Corporate government relations and regulatory affairs teams in fashion, design, manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, banking and tech — monitoring Italian and EU files that affect northern Italy’s industrial base.
  • Trade associations and industry federations representing manufacturers, services and territorial clusters toward Rome and Brussels.
  • Public affairs, communications and management consultancies with EU regulatory practices.
  • Think tanks, foundations and university policy centres active on industrial strategy, cohesion and European economics.
  • NGOs and advocacy groups with Lombardy offices, often paired with Rome or Brussels headquarters.
  • Law firms and advisory networks handling EU competition, state aid, product and sustainability rules.

National political negotiation still centres on Rome; day-to-day EU institutional lobbying still centres on Brussels. Milan’s edge is proximity to company headquarters and finance.

Languages and profiles

Italian is typically required for association and domestic public affairs roles; English is expected for multinational and consultancy work. Common titles include public affairs manager, regulatory affairs specialist, EU affairs adviser and sustainability policy lead.
